correctness.rationale: The conditional expected infected count is exactly a uniform seed reachability sum, and forward-acquaintance vertex probabilities are obtained by averaging reciprocal outgoing degrees. Their difference has an integer Bernstein expansion indexed by every retained arc subset. Exhaustive bitmask enumeration covers all strongly connected loopless digraphs through four vertices and all five-vertex digraphs at p=1. A self-contained C++17 checker reproduced coefficients, complete counts and permutation orbits. At four vertices only 24 relabelings of the seven-arc witness have any positive coefficient and all have p(1-6p-5p^2)/72; at p=1 the five-vertex minimum is eight arcs, one 120-relabeling class with gap 1/20. The finite proof is not extended beyond its quantifiers.

Residual risk is a differently titled finite graph-reliability or intervention result; independent literature review is not claimed.

value.rationale: This gives a tight structural limit for a natural low-information, directed vaccination strategy and separates transmissibility-sensitive failure (four vertices, exactly determined interval) from full-transmission failure (five vertices and an exact sparsity minimum). The property is an observable expected outbreak burden, not an arbitrary integer table, and it isolates a qualitative weakness of sampling downstream contacts when high risk and high spread do not coincide. It is useful as a small complete falsification benchmark for directed intervention heuristics.
